newsitem.title: USA: Zenith posts larger loss, cites big restructuring charges.
newsitem.headline: Zenith posts larger loss, cites big restructuring charges.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp., the struggling TV maker, Tuesday reported a wider loss for the latest quarter, reflecting the impact of $40 million worth of retructuring charges.

The Glenview, Ill.-based company, which faces tough competition from overseas amid declining prices for television prices, said it lost $69.3 million, or $1.05 a share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Dec. 31, compared with a loss of $23.0 million, or 42 cents a share, a year earlier. Sales rose to $427.6 million from $394.7 million.

For the year, Zenith said its loss jumped to $178.0 million, or $2.73 a share, due to charges totalling $80.0 million, on sales of $1.29 billion. That compared with a year-earlier loss of $90.8 million, or $1.85 a share, on sales of $1.27 billion.
"We are confident that the actions we have taken position Zenith for major performance improvements in 1997 and beyond," Peter Willmott, president, said in a statement.

The company said it plans a multi-million-dollar national advertising campaign -- its first in five years -- and expects to achieve revenue growth in the second half of 1997 as it focuses on higher-margin home theatre television systems and new "convergence" television products.
Convergence products include equipment that allows TVs to access the Internet and offer expanded interactive functions.
In addition, Zenith said it expects to begin shipping high-resolution computer display tubes to computer monitor makers by mid-year.
It also will start initial shipments of new digital set-top boxes to telecommunications companies under a five-year, $1.0 billion contract with the Americast consortium that was signed last August.
A Zenith spokesman said the company is not issuing a projection for its first-half revenues.
Zenith said that to support its 1997 business plan, it is seeking financing for its capital investment projects and working capital requirements.
A spokesman said these capital needs total in the "hundreds of millions" of dollars.

It added that existing credit agreements, amended at year-end 1996, continue in place as the company moves toward completing its new financing, which will be supported by its majority stockholder, South Korea's LG Electronic Inc.
Zenith's stock was up 12.5 cents at $9.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
